key_insight: The paper shows that even when embodied RL systems keep raw sensor data on-device, the sequence of transmitted policy gradients can leak the full private trajectory. TRACE exploits temporal dependencies to reconstruct consecutive observation-action data more effectively than single-step attacks.
problem_solved: It addresses the privacy risk in distributed embodied reinforcement learning, where sharing per-step gradients can unintentionally reveal sensitive time-series trajectories from agents operating in the real world.
method: Introduces TRACE (Temporal Reconstruction Attack on Consecutive Encodings), an amortized temporal gradient-inversion attack.
Uses autoregressive reconstruction to recover observation-action sequences step by step from per-step policy gradients.
Exploits temporal structure across consecutive encodings, rather than treating each gradient update independently.
impact: For practitioners, this is a warning that gradient sharing alone does not guarantee privacy in sequential decision-making settings. It highlights the need for stronger defenses when training embodied RL agents in domains like robotics, navigation, and human-interactive systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: private trajectory on device -> gradients sent to server -> TRACE reconstruction output

paper_title: Temporal Gradient Inversion for Private Trajectory Reconstruction in Embodied Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Sudip Bhujel, Shanghao Shi, Ruiquan Huang, Ning Zhang, Yang Xiao
